subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
MWCC GC 1.2.5 family. A FRAME-SIZE DEFICIT PRESENTS IN regnorm AS A FIXED SIX-ROW STRUCTURAL SIGNATURE WITH A SINGLE CAUSE AND A ONE-TOKEN CURE, AND BECAUSE THE SIGNATURE IS MECHANICAL THE WHOLE TU CAN BE CLEARED IN ONE CENSUS INSTEAD OF ONE FUNCTION AT A TIME.

THE SIGNATURE, measured on combat.c::get_attn_pos_8002C9A8: six STRUCTURAL rows, all frame words, all expressing one number - `stwu r1,-176` vs `-128`, `addi r11,r1,176` vs `128` (twice, prologue and epilogue), `stmw r29,124(r1)` vs `76(r1)`, `lmw r29,124(r1)` vs `76(r1)`, `lwz r0,180(r1)` vs `132(r1)`. Every one is the same 48-byte delta. They were 6 of the function's 7 STRUCTURAL rows, so the whole structural residual was ONE missing number.

THE DECISIVE DIAGNOSTIC, and the reason the cure is a single token: if NO r1-relative LOCAL displacement appears in the diff, our locals already sit at the target's offsets, so the missing bytes are not interleaved among them - they are a contiguous block at the TOP of the local frame. Per claim.law.stack-slots-descend-in-declaration-order the top of the local block belongs to the FIRST-declared local, so growing the first declaration by exactly the delta shifts the saved-register area up and moves nothing else. Here `u8 unused[44]` -> `u8 unused[92]` took real 80 -> 66, fresh fuzzy 98.9194 -> 98.9382, and regnorm STRUCTURAL 7 -> 0, with instruction count and opcode multiset unchanged throughout (T372/O372, 0t) - which is exactly why no count-based or multiset-based screen can find this class.

THE CENSUS RESULT THAT MAKES THIS WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN JUST FIXING. After the fix, the same frame-row filter was run across all nine open functions of combat.c (DiffRate, EnemyStartMissile, InitCamera, InitPlayerMissiles, PlayerStartMissile, StandardCamera, screen_limitation, someone_will_be_off_screen, get_attn_pos): every remaining function reported 'frame words agree'. get_attn_pos was the class's ONLY member and the class is now CLOSED for this TU. That is a decided-and-empty result, not an untested one, and it should stop any future lane from opening a frame/pad axis here.

OPERATIONAL RULE. Run the frame-row filter across a TU's whole open roster as the FIRST census after regnorm, before ranking anything by genuine structural rows: it costs one regnorm pass per function and no builds, its members are each a one-token fix, and its non-members are conclusively excluded. Also treat it as a standing rebuttal to any record claiming 'no frame/slot residual' on the strength of equal instruction counts - the record superseded here made exactly that claim about exactly this function while a 48-byte deficit was live, because equal counts and an identical multiset are precisely what a pure frame deficit produces.
